title: Release Pulse: Ops Calendar and Smoke Routine (Q3 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This doc defines a compact, repeatable 'Release Pulse' for Q3 2026: a calendar-driven ops cadence plus a tightly scoped smoke routine to validate production readiness and catch regressions early. Intended as a lightweight working playbook for release leads, on-call SREs, and feature owners.

Principles (short):
- Time-box checks: targeted 10-25 minute checks at each pulse step.
- Observable first: every pulse has at least one metric and one log/tracing check.
- Fast rollback decision boundary: define a single clear binary threshold for rollback.
- Customer impact minimization: schedule risky changes in low-traffic twilight windows where possible.

Pulse taxonomy (how we roll):
- Preflight (T-72 to T-1): progressive validation steps starting at 72h out.
- Launch window (T0 to T+60m): immediate smoke routine and throttled ramp.
- Short-term stabilization (T+1h to T+24h): hourly pulse checks and fast mitigations.
- Day+ stabilization (T+24h to T+72h): daily pulse and metrics regression watch.

High-level calendar template (example week for a medium-risk release):
- T-72 (3 days prior): Release owner posts readiness note, verifies dependent tickets, and attaches runbook. Brief: 10m.
- T-48: Canary deploy to 2% traffic in region A. Perf smoke script run (see Smoke Routine below). 20m.
- T-24: Canary to 10% and cross-region sanity (region B). DB migration dry-run verification. 25m.
- T-4: Final code freeze verification and telemetry gates check. Feature flags prepared. 15m.
- T-0: Production push in 3 waves (1%, 10%, 100%) spaced by 10–20m depending on metric stability. Launch smoke routine run at each wave.
- T+1h, T+3h, T+6h, T+12h, T+24h: Pulse checks (15m each).

Twilight windows and traffic knobs:
- Preferred windows: 02:00–05:00 PT for global infra-affecting releases.
- Throttle knobs: global rate limiter, per-region circuit breaker, per-model capacity cap. Engineers must confirm breakpoints in the rollout config.

Smoke Routine (compact checklist executed at each rollout wave):
1) Endpoint sanity: 3 representative endpoints (generate-response, chat-stream, embeddings) respond within SLA (p50 < configured target). Quick curl + header checks.
2) Health endpoints: service-health, model-manager-health, kv-cache-health => HTTP 200.
3) Telemetry sanity: token throughput and error-rate compared to baseline (check last 15m vs. baseline; fail if > 3x error-rate or token drop > 30%).
4) Latency tail check: p95/p99 in region vs baseline (fail if p99 > baseline + 200ms or relative increase > 40%).
5) Keytrace sample: pick 5 sample traces from each critical flow and confirm no resource-timeout or OOM.
6) Cache hit-rate: KV prefix cache present for common prompt families (> 40% hit-rate expected for warm canary).
7) Dependency fallbacks: verify fall-through to fallback-model or region works by toggling a simulated failure (in staging or controlled canary).
8) Quick quality spot-check: run 5 golden prompts and confirm output shape and no hallucination on critical facts.
9) Ops comms: post inline status to release thread with pass/fail + short rationale.
10) Roll decision: if any of the first 6 checks fail, immediate rollback unless mitigations are trivial and confirmed.

Rollback heuristics (binary gates):
- SEV thresholds that trigger rollback:
  - Customer-facing error rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m AND errors affecting > 10% of requests.
  - Latency p99 > 2x baseline for 10+ minutes and user-visible timeouts.
  - Major downstream degradation (DB or cache errors > 5%).
- If any threshold is met, release lead calls rollback and SRE kicks off mitigation playbook.

Metrics & dashboards to watch (minimal set):
- Requests per second (RPS) by region and model-version
- Error rate (4xx/5xx) by endpoint and model-version
- Token generation throughput and queue length
- Latency percentiles p50/p90/p95/p99
- KV cache hit rate and memory pressure
- GPU utilization and preemption events

Communications timeline (who posts what and when):
- T-72: Release owner posts readiness checklist + linked artifacts
- T-0: Release lead posts start-of-window with expected wave cadence
- Every wave: SRE posts smoke result and decision (pass/fail)
- T+1h: Short status + stabilizing notes
- Post T+24h: Stabilization summary + any follow-ups assigned

Post-release triggers and follow-ups:
- Auto-trigger a short blam-free postmortem if any rollback occurred OR any of these hold: sustained error-rate > 0.2% for 6 hours, or quality-regression alerts exceed threshold for 24h.
- 72h wrap: consolidate telemetry, annotate rollouts in release index, and convert any lingering tickets to action items.

Release Notes draft (to be copied into product release notes template):
- Title: Q3-2026 Release — Release Pulse Enhancements
- Summary: This release updates the Release Pulse cadence and adds a compact smoke routine to reduce noisy rollouts and speed rollback decisions. Includes improvements to telemetry gates and rollout orchestration knobs.
- Notable changes:
  - Introduced 'pulse' calendar templates for standardized preflight and post-release checks (RINF-3421).
  - Added automated smoke scripts that exercise generation, chat streaming, and embeddings endpoints.
  - New latency/quality gates in console rollouts and tighter default throttle profiles.
- Impact: Ops will run an explicit smoke routine at each rollout wave; this should reduce time-to-detect regressions and decrease rollbacks caused by missed metrics.
- Rollout plan: Staged rollout using 3 waves across regions with telemetry gates.
- Known issues:
  - Canary cache warmup can take up to 18 minutes for large prompt families (workaround: pre-warm with golden prompts).
  - Edge-region telemetry sampling may undercount p99 in first 30 minutes; we flag but do not auto-rollback on sampling-only anomalies.

Appendix A — Quick command snippets:
- Curl generation endpoint: curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"prompt":"test"}' | jq '.duration'
- Smoke script run (local): ./scripts/smoke/run_smoke.sh --wave 1 --region us-west1

Appendix B — Roles & responsibilities (pulse-owner model):
- Release owner: coordinates feature owners, signs off preflight, owns release notes.
- Release lead: runs the rollout, triggers rollbacks, assigns mitigations.
- SRE on-shift: executes smoke routine, confirms telemetry, runs rollback playbook if needed.
- Feature owner(s): provide golden prompts, validate quality spot-check.

Open questions / items to finalize:
- Exact token-rate delta thresholds for low-risk vs medium-risk releases (proposal: 15% / 30%).
- Where to surface the pulse calendar templates in Console (console roadmap ticket required).
- Add a synthetic health check that specifically measures model warmup time across quantized variants.

Quick action items for this doc (next 72h):
1) Priya to convert smoke script steps to runnable playbooks (JIRA RINF-3472).
2) Maya to wire a minimal 'pulse' calendar template in shared calendar and link from console (CONFLUENCE-RELEASE-PULSE-001).
3) Liam to add a rollout flag that enforces p99 guardrails in the orchestration layer (GITHUB-PR-6721).

Last notes:
This is intentionally concise — the goal is to make release checks fast, observable, and decisive. Feedback welcome; we should iterate this doc after three live runs and one postmortem.
